 Piccoli and Enem are close to returning to Parma. The Ukrainian must convince Palladino and the club, especially considering the prospects: his salary could be a factor.

 Facebook X WhatsApp Print Monza is a test of maturity: for Bologna, who after three consecutive away wins face the ultimate test at home to definitively relaunch their position in the standings, and also for Artem Dovbyk . The Ukrainian arrived seeking a revitalization after his tendon reconstruction surgery last January, as the highest-paid player in the squad, but he has become the last in the rotation, behind Piccoli, Dovbyk, and even behind Odgaard as a false nine. In short, for Dovbyk, it's now or never, one might say: because for Parma, before the break, Bologna hopes to have at least one of Piccoli and Enem back, if not both, and above all, January is approaching.
 What's the point of keeping a third striker worth €3 million? And what's the point of Roma leaving him on the bench at Bologna, risking his value depreciating even further compared to the €17 million he earned on his summer loan with an option to buy, considering they paid €40 for Dovbyk? The Ukrainian striker is perhaps one of the hottest topics at Bologna, especially since the Palladino treatment is bearing the desired fruit in terms of his play, his league position, and even the revival of individual players. Mbangula was the brightest star at San Siro, Libra came on very well at Cagliari, Amondarain was relaunched on the right, also in Sardinia, and Cambiaghi is rediscovering his dazzling form.
 Orso also scored against Lecce, as did Enem, and Odgaard has been the man of providence in recent matches. Add to that the fact that the coach has given chances in recent matches even to those who seemed to be forgotten, like Vitik, Heggem, and Helland, and so few individual players are missing from the list: Moro, of course, but also, if not especially, Dovbyk, the man with the highest salary in the squad, with a net salary of €3 million, €2,5 million of which is paid by the Rossoblu club. Palladino had already made it clear in the last week that he expected a change of pace. The request was followed by a face-to-face meeting.
 Will Dovbyk be available against Monza? "Yes," Palladino said, "he's been pushing harder this week. We even had a meeting, and he's trying to implement what I asked of him. I've seen signs of recovery. He's not fit enough to last 90 minutes, but he's available." We'll see him against Monza: it remains to be seen whether he'll start or play during the match, as seems more likely but not certain. One thing is certain. Bologna is trying to bring Piccoli and Enem back for Parma: while Monza isn't a last-minute call, for Dovbyk, also given the face-to-face meeting between the striker and Palladino, it's very close. Also because Bologna is relaunching itself with its young players: Casale and Bernardeschi (penalty) scored against Cagliari, but considering Mbangula's three goals at San Siro and those of Orsolini and Enem against Lecce, four of the eight goals scored (including Bartesaghi's own goal) in the last three wins have been scored by Under-23s.
